coverage.main: Read all twenty pages of arXiv 1911.07140 (ICLR 2020 camera-ready header): Sections 1-5, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-4 and Appendices A-C (per-class targeted results, untargeted ImageNet, ensembles, generator trained on other data, hyperparameter sweeps, CombOpt comparison, Google Cloud Vision, architectures and hyperparameters).
coverage.supplement: Appendices are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read.
coverage.excluded_results: All reported results are score-based query attacks on the target (up to 50,000 queries): TREMBA searches a generator's embedding learned on source networks, and Trans-NES/Trans-P-RGF start from transferred perturbations. Success-rate-versus-query curves count an example as succeeding at one query if its starting point already fools the target, but no separate zero-query transfer rate is reported.

f1.evidence: Target clean accuracies are mentioned (about 99% on MNIST), but no transferred-example evaluation exists.

f2.evidence: 'Only correctly classified images were counted towards success rate and average queries', recorded as positive setup evidence for the query attacks; no transfer denominator exists.

f3.evidence: Success is defined for the query attack within the query limit.

f5.evidence: Explicit L-infinity bounds (e.g., 0.2 on MNIST) are recorded as setup evidence for query attacks.

f6.evidence: Code is linked (github.com/TransEmbedBA/TREMBA), but with no transfer configuration it is neither a transfer recomputability success nor a failure.

artifact_checks.result: Repository linked in the paper; not cloned or executed; not evaluated as a transfer artifact.

bounds_exclusion.reason: Only query-attack success rates on the attacked target are reported.

limitations: Transfer-prior query attacks are classified as out of scope, consistent with ranks 19 and 43; an independent recoder could flag the one-query success counts as an implicit transfer outcome.
